Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths:"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45]"}}

If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -n 0.8 -d 500`, annealing part"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -n 0.8 -d 500`, annealing part only): 63.485 / 63.170 →"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). If the insertion were split between primers, the reverse primer's 5' tail would coincidentally base-pair with the template, extending its effective annealing footprint to 46 nt (violating the ≤45 rule) and creating a primer overlap. Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -n 0.8 -d 500`, annealing part only): 63.485 / 63.170 → both in [58, 72] ✓\n- |ΔTm| = 0.315 ≤ 5 ✓"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -n 0.8 -d 500`, annealing part only): 63.485 / 63.170 → both in [58, 72] ✓\n- |ΔTm| = 0.315 ≤ 5 ✓\n- Primers are back-to-back (no gap/overlap) at the insertion boundary ✓\n- Reconstructing"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`). Placing the whole insertion in the forward tail avoids this — the forward tail's last base (`a`) mismatches the upstream flank (`g`), so neither primer has spurious extension.\n\n**Constraint verification (all PASS):**\n- Anneal lengths: 16 and 44 → both in [15, 45] ✓\n- Tm (oligotm `-tp 1 -sc 1 -mv 50 -dv 2 -n 0.8 -d 500`, annealing part only): 63.485 / 63.170 → both in [58, 72] ✓\n- |ΔTm| = 0.315 ≤ 5 ✓\n- Primers are back-to-back (no gap/overlap) at the insertion boundary ✓\n- Reconstructing the plasmid from the primers reproduces the output sequence exactly ✓\n- No 15-mer of the insertion appears elsewhere in the input (no off-target annealing) ✓\n- Forward primer listed first; file saved as `/app/primers.fasta` ✓"}}

Since there is only one insertion site, the **minimum number of primer pairs is 1**.\n\n**Primer design (Q5 SDM, back-to-back amplification of the whole plasmid):**\n\n| | Sequence (5'→3') | Total | Anneal part | Anneal len | Tm (°C) | 3' clamp |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| **Forward** | `agtagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaa`**`agcaagggcgaggagc`** | 55 nt | bold = input[213..229] | 16 | 63.485 | C |\n| **Reverse** | `catatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttctag` | 44 nt | revcomp(input[169..213]) | 44 | 63.170 | G |\n\n- The forward primer carries the entire 39-nt insertion as its 5' (non-annealing) tail; its 16-nt 3' end anneals to the GC-rich EGCP downstream flank.\n- The reverse primer is pure annealing (no tail); its 44-nt 3' end anneals to the AT-rich upstream UTR flank.\n\n**Why the insertion lives entirely in the forward primer:** The insertion's first base (`a`) happens to equal the downstream flank's first base (`a`).
